candidates.summary: FastAggregateVerifyExcluding's stated obligations (every excluded key a proven member, every member PoP-proven) do not bind excluded to the cleared participation bits, so a realm that thresholds on sync_committee_bits as Ethereum's light-client spec does accepts one member's signature as full participation
candidates.failure_scenario: Committee of 16 (512 on mainnet), attacker is one ordinary sync-committee member. The update sets every participation bit, lists the other 15 members as excluded (each a real member with a valid Merkle branch, so the doc's membership obligation at bls12381.gno:50-52 and bls12381.go:71-74 holds, and every key is honestly generated, so PoP holds), and carries the attacker's own signature over a forged header. X_fastAggregateVerifyExcluding returns true (aggregate minus excluded is the attacker's key) and the bitfield reads 16/16, past the 2/3 supermajority. The ADR repeats the same membership-only obligation (pr6375_bls12381_native.md:35-37, 56). It extends moul's excluded-membership thread: the obligation that thread asked for, now in the doc, is necessary but not sufficient; the doc must also say that signers are counted as committee size minus excluded, each excluded key bound by its branch to a distinct position whose bit is clear.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/topic1-excluding-bitfield_test.go gnovm/stdlibs/crypto/bls12381/ && go test -count=1 -timeout 2m -run TestTopic1ExcludingBitfield -v ./gnovm/stdlibs/crypto/bls12381/ : expect X_fastAggregateVerifyExcluding true with 16/16 bits and 15 proven-member excluded keys; then grep bls12381.gno/bls12381.go/ADR for any obligation tying excluded to the participation bits or to the signer count (none at head)
candidates.evidence: membership of all 15 excluded keys: proven; bits set: 16/16; 2/3 threshold met: true; X_fastAggregateVerifyExcluding: true; signers by excluded: 1 -- FAIL: a single member's signature over a forged header passes as 16/16 participation with both documented obligations met

candidates.summary: No Ethereum or IETF vector pins the canonical-encoding rejections the natives inherit from gnark: x equal to or above p, infinity flag with a nonzero payload, b and a flags together, missing c flag, for keys and signatures; every Go-suite signature is generated by gnark itself
candidates.failure_scenario: The only malformed-encoding case is 'garbage signature' (one byte flipped at index 10); infinity and lengths are the rest. A gnark-crypto bump or a switch of decoder that reduced x mod p or ignored the payload of an infinity encoding would admit a second encoding of a committee key or signature, which Ethereum clients reject, and nothing in bls12381_test.go or bls12381_test.gno turns red. At head all 13 G1 and 15 G2 deserialization vectors, 12 fast_aggregate_verify, 28 verify, 9 sign (under ethDST) and 4 hash_to_G2 vectors of ethereum/bls12-381-tests v0.1.2 and consensus-spec-tests v1.5.0 agree, so the harness can be imported as the test.
